evidence: Quint. 1.5.50: intrō et intus locī adverbia
Prisc. p. 1003 P.: pars ōrātiōnis indēclīnābilis, cujus significātiō verbīs adjicitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The word “added to the verb”, ad verbum. Its kinds go in the genitive: adverbium locī, of place (Quintilian’s phrase), temporis, of time, numerī, of number (Traupman 231). Adverbs do not decline: sunt indēclīnābilia (Traupman 232).

phrases.latin: hoc amplius intrō et intus locī adverbia, eō tamen intus et intrō sum soloecismī sunt
phrases.english: moreover intrō and intus are adverbs of place, yet eō intus and intrō sum are mistakes

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 220, p. 231, p. 232, p. 245.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
